test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Sept, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens were adopted from the Constitution of which country?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Soviet Union**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens were adopted from the Constitution of the **Soviet Union**.
 
• These duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A.
 
• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed in the Constitution of India.
 
• The Fundamental Duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have certain duties to perform towards their country and society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **42nd Amendment**, also known as the "Mini-Constitution," brought about several changes, including the addition of the Fundamental Duties.
 
• These duties emphasize the importance of national unity, integrity, and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all Indians.
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties was intended to bring about a sense of moral obligation among citizens to uphold the spirit of patriotism and to contribute to the nation's well-being.
